$comment: Input gates. This is the only definition of the rules: public/js/gates.js (browser and node) and tools/gates.py (pipeline) both read this file and contain no thresholds of their own. Rules run in order; the first one that fires decides the level. Only level 'ok' may enter scoring. A rule with 'applies_from' is skipped while the sequence is shorter than that. A threshold may be a number or {absolute, fraction_of_requested}, which resolves to max(absolute, ceil(fraction * requested)) when the requested count is known and to 'absolute' otherwise. 'observed' records the extreme value of the statistic across every real sample the gates were set against (tools/samples plus the 468 upstream ModelTrace rows), so the margin between real data and the threshold is visible here and re-checked by tools/tests/test_gates.py.

rules.message: No numbers between 1 and 355 were found in the answer.
Every number is the same. A model asked for random numbers never does this.
The numbers are sorted. A counted or sorted list is not a model's answer.
The numbers move in a fixed step. That is a pattern, not a sample.

observed.note: set by tools/tests/test_gates.py --write-observed. The threshold cannot be higher: upstream claude-sonnet-5 query-17 (in the bank) has 28 distinct values in 317 numbers and repeats the same twelve-number runs for 64% of its length, so neither a stricter unique-ratio rule nor a repeated-block rule survives the real data.

rules.message: Fewer than one number in twenty is distinct. That is a handful of values cycled, not a sample.

observed.note: ModelTrace's own acceptance rule (analyzeGlobalOutputs in fingerprint-core.js): max(80, ceil(0.55 * expected)). Kept identical so the gate and the core never disagree about what is long enough.

rules.message: The answer is too short to score. Paste the complete reply, or run the challenge again.

stats.$comment: Definitions the two evaluators implement. length: count of parsed numbers. unique_count: distinct values. unique_ratio: unique_count / min(length, value_max - value_min + 1), so an answer longer than the value range is not penalised for the repeats it cannot avoid. monotone_fraction: over consecutive pairs, the larger of the non-decreasing share and the non-increasing share (a sorted list scores 1). arithmetic_fraction: share of consecutive pairs whose absolute difference equals the most common absolute difference (a fixed-step list scores 1, a zigzag of one step size too). min_length: the resolved too_short threshold for this input. All fractions are 0 when there are fewer than two numbers.
